Heard.
Admit.
By consent of the learned Counsel for the parties, the matter is taken up for the final disposal.

2. This is an application seeking to quash the First Information Report (for short-"FIR") bearing Crime No. 331/2022, registered with Police Station Akot, and the Charge sheet arising out of the said FIR for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 294, 420, 468, 471, 504 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code (for short -"IPC") and Sections 3(1)(r)(s), 3(2), (5a) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989.

sentences.text: 3. Mr. Sirpurkar, the learned Counsel for the applicants, and Mr. Chande, the learned Counsel for non-applicant No. 2, have submitted that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties.
Accordingly, applicant No.1 and non-applicant No. 2 have filed joint compromise pursis dated 12.12.2024 and their respective affidavit along with a copy of the divorce petition they filed.
In the pursis, non-applicant No. 2 has stated that she does not want to proceed with the prosecution against the applicants.
A gist of the case is that the marriage of applicant No. 1 with non-applicant No. 2 was solemnized on 07.12.2021 as per rites and rituals prevailing in their community.
Applicant Nos. 2 to 4 are the in-laws of non-applicant No. 2.

On account of matrimonial discord on 11.06.2022, non-applicant No. 2 lodged a report against applicants with Akot Police Station alleging that the applicants subjected her to cruelty on account of the demand for dowry, cheated her stating false age of applicant No.1 and harassed on the count of her caste.

Based on the complaint, the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 294, 420, and 504 r/w 34 of the IPC and Sections 3(1)(r)(s), 3(2),
(5a) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act came to be registered vide FIR No. 331/2022.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. Being aggrieved by the registration of FIR and filing of the Charge Sheet, applicants filled this application to quash and set aside the same since the allegations made therein do not constitute the commission of any of the offences.
6. Perusal of the record shows that during the pendency of the application, the dispute has been redressed amicably between 4 apl979.2023..odt the applicants and the non-applicant No.2.

Accordingly, applicant No. 1 and the non-applicant No. 2 have filed a copy of the Divorce Petition Santosh @ Sonu S/O. Chandrakant Saoji ... vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso, Ps, Akot City, ... on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102051527/

sentences.text:
and compromise/Joint pursis in that regard.
7.
Today, applicant No.1, non-applicant No. 2, along with her brother, are present before the Court.
Their respective counsel identifies them.
Applicant No.1 and non-applicant No. 2 have reiterated the contents of the Pursis and their respective affidavit.

As per the settlement pursis, applicant No.1 has agreed to pay Rs. 1,50,000/- to non-applicant No. 2 towards full and final settlement amount/
permanent alimony, out of which she has received Rs. 50,000/- from the applicants.
The applicants agreed to pay Rs. 100000/- to her in the divorce proceedings bearing HMP No. 147/2024.
A copy of the divorce petition and the joint pursis on record has been filed.

Non-applicant No. 2 in the affidavit stated that from 31/03/2022, she has been residing separately, the matter has been settled between her and the applicants, and she has received Rs. 50,000/- from applicant No. 1.
It is further stated that she agreed to withdraw the domestic violence proceedings pending before the concerned Court.
Thus, it seems that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties.
Pursuant to the settlement, non-applicant No. 2 also received Rs. 50,000/- towards permanent alimony from applicant No. 1.

She has voluntarily given no objection to quashing the FIR bearing crime No.
331/22 and the Charge Sheet before this Court.
Moreover, the nature of the offence is neither heinous nor anti-social, but the same arises out of the marital dispute.
Therefore, in our view, there is no reason to continue with the prosecution.
9. In the wake of the above, it would be proper to allow the application in terms of the settlement as it would not cause prejudice to any of the parties.
10. In the background above, we are satisfied that the case is made out to exercise our inherent powers to secure the ends of justice and to prevent abuse of the process of the law.

Hence, we pass the following order:
(i) The Criminal Application is allowed.

(ii) We hereby quash and set aside FIR bearing Crime No. 331/2021 registered with Police Station Akot and filing of the Charge Sheet pursuant to the said FIR for the offence punishable under Sections 498-A, 294, 420, 468, 6 apl979.2023..odt 471, 504 r/w 34 of the IPC and Sections 3(1)(r)(s), 3(2), (5a) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
